pull_requests.title: Finish the per-machine LUKS re-key: recovery key, drive password, factory reset and boot check
pull_requests.head: 5e6303ec1961718059b524f9cd80e79fd1aa35bc

commits.message:
Add an Apple Silicon LUKS recovery keyslot after first-boot re-key.

On Macs the throwaway ESP key is shredded, rd.luks.key= is dropped via update-grub, and a 48-character base32 recovery passphrase is shown once.

Keep login and LUKS passphrases in sync on Apple Silicon.

The Intel Limine path is unchanged; the Apple GRUB+sd-encrypt branch updates the disk key and the owner/root login password together.

Stage an ESP LUKS keyfile for Apple Silicon factory reset.

@factory restore still re-keys the volume; on Macs the throwaway key lives on the ESP and mkinitcpio, update-grub, and update-m1n1 rebuild the boot chain.

Check GRUB, crypttab, and sd-encrypt when the Apple Silicon root is LUKS.

Unencrypted roots keep the existing boot-check; after provisioning rd.luks.key= must be gone.

Finish Apple LUKS re-key by rebuilding initramfs and marking encrypt.state.

The throwaway key lives on the ext4 Boot partition; recovery is shown once and acknowledged by typing a fixed phrase.

Re-arm both first-boot markers on Apple factory reset.

The sealed @factory snapshot keeps neither marker nor install.conf nor encrypt.state; the throwaway key is staged on Boot.

Fail Apple boot-check while throwaway LUKS unlock remains after provisioning.

Once first-boot markers are gone, rd.luks.key=, the Boot keyfile, extra keyslots, or a non-finished encrypt.state all fail.

Show the recovery key before Apple LUKS re-key is final.

Retries reuse recorded keyslots, cryptsetup failure no longer desyncs login, and a mapper root without crypttab is a failure.

Make Apple LUKS re-key idempotent and crash-resumable.

Retries reuse recorded owner and recovery slots instead of adding more, finalisation continues from phase=rekeyed, and factory-reset only writes the Boot keyfile after rebuilds succeed.

Keep the reset unlock after a successful factory reset and record the slot cryptsetup used

The EXIT trap revoked the reset keyslot and Boot keyfile even when the reset
had activated; it now revokes only an uncommitted reset. The throwaway slot is
the one cryptsetup actually filled (the lowest free), the live Boot partition's
encrypt.state goes back to configured so the next owner setup re-keys, the
recovery key is refused from the background worker, drive-password keeps
cryptsetup's diagnostics, and the [[ ]] quoting follows this repository's rule.
Reopen the encryption state only after the factory system is activated
Point the factory reset test at a live crypttab and test the post-activation state reopen
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into e/T4c
Accept the mtree verification the boot check now runs in the LUKS boot-check test
Stage the Aurora release identity the boot check binds the running kernel to in the LUKS test

pull_requests.title: Mac image first-boot VM harness
pull_requests.head: e2b1076b0c6d8c01b7cb93cfa3d3dc05442e1d39

commits.message:
Mac image first-boot VM harness

Boots a built Mac image in a KVM guest twice over: install.conf encrypt=0
(first boot leaves the root plain and arms owner provisioning) and no
install.conf (in-place LUKS2 conversion, GRUB and initramfs regenerated,
root switched to the mapper, then a second boot through sd-encrypt). The
Aurora kernel cannot run on QEMU virt, so the guest boots a generic Arch
Linux ARM kernel with an initramfs built inside the image root from the
image's own hooks. This is the recipe that found the two encrypt-unit bugs
fixed in omarchy-pkgs #170, kept as a script with evidence output.
README: the harness addresses disks by path
harness: track loop devices outside command substitution; hold members to the signed IMAGE; preflight and evidence nits
harness: fail loudly on a missing PROVENANCE payload line or IMAGE input digest; README wrap
harness: read the stopped guest's disks without journal replay
harness: the overlay upper dir is root-owned, remove the run directory with sudo
harness: replay the stopped guest's journals (fsynced btrfs writes live in the tree-log)
harness: let the ESP writeback land before stopping the guest

pull_requests.title: Apple Silicon: snapper update snapshots and a gated snapshot restore
pull_requests.head: 1dd44950964f28cf52ece089526d59a6db174cdb

commits.message:
Apple Silicon: snapper update snapshots and a gated snapshot restore

Apple Silicon installs never had snapper: the package was excluded and
install/config/snapper.sh skipped, so `omarchy update` silently took no
snapshot (exit 127) and nothing could restore one. snapper is now in the
Apple package set and snapper.sh runs everywhere: an image build bakes the
retention policy and the cleanup timer without touching the build root
(create-config would nest a /.snapshots subvolume the image copy flattens),
a deferred first-boot step creates the /.snapshots subvolume on the Mac,
and a migration brings installed Macs to the same state. The Limine sync
unit stays x86 only.

Restore on Macs cannot use snapper rollback (fstab and GRUB name subvol=@)
or Limine's tool. omarchy-snapshot restore now dispatches to
omarchy-mac-snapshot-restore, which stages a writable clone of the snapshot
on the top level, moves the live /.snapshots collection into it so snapper
keeps its numbering, writes a recovery record on the plaintext Boot
partition, renames the roots the way the factory reset does, and reboots.
The next boot verifies the restore before the kept previous root may be
pruned. The rename pair is not crash-safe, so the command is gated to
machines that opted in with /var/lib/omarchy/snapshot-restore.enabled;
mismatched kernels, swap layouts, pending provisioning and a kept previous
root are refused before anything is touched.

Apple Silicon restore: recover a half-done swap, prune only after the verifying boot

Review findings. A failed second rename left no @: the current root now
gets its name back before anything else is unwound, and the record stays
whenever the unwind is incomplete. prune-previous checked only the running
root's pending marker, which the restore writes into the clone, so it
could delete the still-running previous root before the reboot; it now
requires the record to say finished and the running root to be the
restored clone the record names. The finish worker fails closed when
snapper is missing or the record cannot be updated, and requires /boot
mounted. The first-boot leaf removes only an empty stub directory. The
kernel on /boot is identified through the installed Apple kernel package
(omarchy-hw-apple-kernel, /boot/vmlinuz-<package>) rather than by any
modules directory with a pkgbase.

Apple Silicon restore: keep the record until recovery is complete, prove the running root

Review findings. The record is removed only by the run that wrote it and
only once every recovery step succeeded; a refusal for a kept root leaves
an earlier record alone. prune-previous requires a finished record and
checks the mounted root's subvolume id against the clone the record
names. The finish worker fails closed without a record. A snapshot from
before the restore worker shipped is refused, since its next boot could
not verify itself. The kernel on /boot must be byte-identical to the
vmlinuz the matching modules directory ships, not merely present. The
helpers replace command -v, and the record heredoc declares its
expansions.

pull_requests.title: Apple Silicon: bootable snapshots in the GRUB menu through grub-btrfs
pull_requests.head: 1494ea98161759ad4fd6a456df326dac8317f551

commits.message:
Apple Silicon: bootable snapshots in the GRUB menu through grub-btrfs

Tier 2 of the Apple Silicon snapshot support: grub-btrfs joins the Apple
package set and a new omarchy-mac-snapshot-menu writes its configuration,
runs the generator into /boot/grub/grub-btrfs.cfg and adds the "Omarchy
snapshots" submenu include to grub.cfg once, through the Asahi update-grub
(which also resets grubenv and re-copies the EFI GRUB, so never per
snapshot). There is no grub-btrfsd: omarchy-snapshot refreshes the menu
after each snapshot, the restore tools after pruning and verification, and
the omarchy-mac-boot kernel hook after a kernel change.

The kernel lives on the ext4 /boot outside every snapshot, so only
snapshots that carry the modules of the kernel on /boot are offered; the
rest, @, @factory and the staging or kept roots are hidden. Snapshots are
read-only; the omarchy-mac-boot initrd unit overlays a tmpfs on them for
the session.

Apple Silicon snapshot menu: hide kept roots by exact name, identify the /boot kernel

grub-btrfs reads IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH as "prefix/*", not as a string prefix,
so staging and kept roots are now enumerated from the top level and listed
by exact name. The kernel on /boot is identified through the installed
Apple kernel package like the restore does.
Validation checklist: the GRUB snapshot submenu and snapshot boots
Apple Silicon snapshot menu: match the /boot image against the modules directory's vmlinuz
Snapshot menu: declare the config heredoc's expansions

pull_requests.title: Snapper: skip configuration on a root that is not btrfs
pull_requests.head: ea2894457a1f38206bbbdb95f38a17e094b829bb

commits.message:
Snapper: skip configuration on a root that is not btrfs

install/config/snapper.sh now runs on Apple Silicon too, and the VM
acceptance guest installs onto a generic image whose root is not btrfs:
snapper's create-config failed there and took the config phase down with
it, so the fresh install never completed. A non-btrfs root now skips the
config, the timer and the first-boot /.snapshots step with a message;
every real Omarchy layout is btrfs.

pull_requests.title: Apple Silicon: readable GRUB font and an unbounded root-device wait
pull_requests.head: 1845f6d74dbf7ddbb9e71516dc15ad8db23d56fb

commits.message:
Apple Silicon: readable GRUB font and an unbounded root-device wait

GRUB drew its menu with the 16-pixel unicode font on a native-resolution
panel, which the owner could not read, and an unattended boot of an
encrypted Mac gave up on the root device after systemd's 90 s default and
sat in the initrd's emergency mode (root locked, "Press Enter") instead of
waiting at the passphrase prompt; the M2 Max spent a night there. The new
install/hardware/apple/grub-console.sh renders a 28-pixel Liberation Mono
font for GRUB, points GRUB_FONT at it, appends
rootflags=x-systemd.device-timeout=0 to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX (systemd
concatenates repeated rootflags, so the initrd's sysroot device job waits
without limit), and regenerates GRUB once. It runs at first boot for image
installs (deferred hardware step) and through a migration on installed
Macs.

GRUB console leaf: one authoritative assignment, regeneration owed until it succeeds

Review findings: a later active assignment would have overridden the
edited first one, and a failed update-grub left the defaults reading as
configured so the retry skipped it. The leaf now keeps the effective
(last) value, collapses the key to one line, and records a pending
regeneration until update-grub succeeds.

pull_requests.title: Apple Silicon: the Omarchy GRUB theme and a splash-only boot
pull_requests.head: 056a250d4fc047c1c9d3953f8b407755c698bcb2

commits.message:
Apple Silicon: the Omarchy GRUB theme and a splash-only boot

The GRUB console leaf now gives Macs the x86 Limine look: a gfxmenu theme
with the Tokyo Night backdrop, the green "Omarchy Bootloader" title and
Liberation fonts rendered at install, the menu shown for three seconds
like x86, and the efi_gop backend the arm64 GRUB ships (no more
"efi_uga.mod not found"). The boot after the menu is the splash alone:
Plymouth forced its text view because the device tree registers the
serial console (plymouth.ignore-serial-consoles fixes that, verified on
the M1 Pro), and 10_linux's "Loading Linux ..." echoes are guarded behind
a quiet kernel line, with the original kept under /var/lib/omarchy/backups
rather than in grub.d where an executable copy runs as a second
generator. A new migration runs the leaf again on Macs that took the
earlier one.

GRUB console leaf: install only a complete 10_linux guard, fail closed on fonts

Review findings: a partially matching 10_linux could end up with the
marker but only one guard; the transformed script is now checked for both
guards and both guarded echoes and parsed with sh before it replaces the
original. A font grub-mkfont cannot render no longer activates the theme
or GRUB_FONT. The test executes the guarded heredoc under sh for both a
quiet and a loud kernel line.

pull_requests.title: Apple Silicon: Limine is the boot loader
pull_requests.head: f8010dbd1a278bda59016ab6d1ffde3238ecbb06

commits.message:
Experiment: Limine in front of U-Boot on the M1 Pro

Not for merging: records the configuration, the deploy/rollback script and
the findings of booting Aurora Linux through Limine 12.9 on Apple Silicon
(boots; kernel copies must live on the ESP; what an integration would need).
Experiment: UKIs boot through Limine on the M1 Pro; entry tool needs an aarch64 patch

Experiment: Apple Limine leaf driving the x86 tooling on the M1 Pro

Gated by /var/lib/omarchy/limine.enabled. Puts Limine at BOOTAA64.EFI,
keeps GRUB as a recovery entry and retargets Asahi's update-grub to it,
writes /etc/default/limine for an ESP at /boot/efi with GRUB's kernel
command line, installs Omarchy's limine.conf with a 3 s timeout, then
limine-update (UKI with the aarch64 systemd-stub, entries) and
limine-snapper-sync. Needs limine-mkinitcpio-hook 1.36.0-2 (aarch64
entries).
Experiment leaf: recovery entry after the Omarchy block so default_entry 2 is the kernel

Apple Silicon: Limine boot integration behind the limine.enabled gate

The limine-boot leaf activates Limine only after limine-update produced a
menu that boots the kernel's UKI: GRUB is regenerated into grub-aa64.efi
first (never copied from the U-Boot slot), the recovery entry is re-placed
after the Omarchy block on every run, and a pacman hook redeploys the
packaged Limine since limine-install does nothing on aarch64.

/etc/default/grub stays the source of the kernel command line:
omarchy-mac-limine-cmdline derives KERNEL_CMDLINE[default] from it (one
merged rootflags with subvol=@) before every UKI rebuild, and
omarchy-mac-boot-update regenerates GRUB, then Limine, for the re-key, the
fresh installer and the factory reset. omarchy-snapshot uses the x86 tooling
on a Limine Mac (limine-snapper-restore, the sync watcher), and
omarchy-mac-boot-sync rebuilds the ext4 /boot for the GRUB recovery entry
when a Limine restore leaves it behind the running kernel. The boot check
verifies the UKI, the entry's root and LUKS mapping, and the ESP's Limine.
apple-limine: README for the integrated state

omarchy-mac-boot-sync: leave a pending kernel update alone

/boot is consistent while its kernel has modules in this root; only a
kernel with no modules here (a restored root) is rebuilt from the running one.

Limine leaf: full rollback on a failed activation; staged Limine deploy

A failed activation restores GRUB's update target and regenerates GRUB
into the U-Boot slot, not only the Limine defaults. The ESP's Limine is
staged and synced before the rename. omarchy-mac-boot-sync runs
/usr/bin/mkinitcpio so the wrapper's UKI rebuild cannot hide a failed
initramfs, and a missing root UUID fails the command line derivation.
apple-limine: record the verified restore cycle

Apple Silicon: the channel menu offers stable and rc only

Edge is the Aurora testing kernel lane (lab Macs move there with
omarchy-apple-silicon-channel switch) and dev an upstream source checkout;
neither is a Mac user channel. The menu hides both on a Mac and
omarchy-channel-set refuses them.

Limine Macs: no GRUB in the boot, no recovery entry, no /boot resync

Limine is the boot loader on Apple Silicon. The Asahi update-grub is
retargeted to an unused file under /boot/grub; the menu is Omarchy's and
its snapshots; omarchy-mac-boot-update, the boot check and the grub-btrfs
menu skip GRUB on a Limine Mac. The experiment scripts and the /boot
resync unit are gone; the design note moves to docs/apple-silicon-limine.md.

Apple Silicon: Limine for new installs and installed Macs

The Apple manifest installs limine, limine-mkinitcpio-hook,
limine-snapper-sync and the silent uboot-asahi; the image build ships the
limine.enabled gate so the deferred limine-boot leaf activates Limine at
first boot; a migration brings installed Macs over; the platform contract
names Limine as the boot backend.

Limine Macs: migration registered, reset keeps Limine, fatal hook failure

The Limine migration is in the Apple disposition table; the factory reset
starts the ESP's Limine menu over and verifies the rebuilt entries; a
missing root UUID aborts the UKI rebuild from the pre-hook (exit 100); the
GRUB-era root swap refuses to run on a Limine Mac.

pull_requests.title: Fresh installer: GRUB's configuration is verified by content
pull_requests.head: a3595846e65f53e630ec731b11c7d83eb74ccba1

commits.message:
Fresh installer: GRUB's configuration is verified by content, not digest

The GRUB console leaf regenerates grub.cfg during system setup (quiet
boot, theme), so a byte-identical grub.cfg is no longer the invariant of
a fresh install. The installer and the VM harness now require that the
regenerated configuration boots the installed kernel; the kernel image
stays protected by digest. VM acceptance of the Limine candidate failed
on the old check.

pull_requests.title: Fresh installer: a resume accepts the recorded GRUB configuration
pull_requests.head: 42acab023f4fcdc0507e67eb545eda8fa78ddb0d

commits.message:
Fresh installer: a resume accepts the recorded GRUB configuration

An install interrupted before the console leaf ran still has the
original grub.cfg, which need not name the kernel yet; the resume accepts
the digest recorded at the checkpoint or a configuration that boots the
installed kernel. The end of the install still requires the latter.

pull_requests.title: VM acceptance: the guest keeps its own boot configuration
pull_requests.head: aae41397e4bedabbbd5b43b6d6233af489ac0408

commits.message:
VM acceptance: the guest keeps its own boot configuration

Omarchy's GRUB console leaf regenerates grub.cfg during the install, and
the result boots the Asahi kernel, which the QEMU guest cannot run: the
guest never came back from the reboot. The harness now keeps Omarchy's
configuration as evidence, checks it boots the Asahi kernel, and puts the
guest's own configuration back before the reboot, the way it already
keeps the guest kernel image.

pull_requests.title: Release records for the Limine boot candidate 2949b88c
pull_requests.head: bec0589b3664fdaa2ef7c082bfea0402b0441956

commits.message:
Release records for the Limine boot candidate 2949b88c

VM acceptance on the M1 Pro and the hardware evidence for the three boot
packages (limine-mkinitcpio-hook, omarchy-mac-boot, uboot-asahi) that
package channel 13 and runtime channel 54 published.

pull_requests.title: Limine leaf: roll back on any failure, and refuse without the menu
pull_requests.head: 1aa0b372d153dfded28456cba8ef9b8e902e227f

commits.message:
Limine leaf: roll back on any failure, and refuse without the menu

Activating Limine on the M2 Max stopped halfway: the Omarchy menu template
is not on an Apple Silicon Mac, and the leaf had already retargeted GRUB's
update and written Limine's defaults before the step that needed it. The
leaf now returns before touching anything when the template is missing and
rolls back from an unexpected failure too, and the migration verifies the
boot files before it counts as done.

pull_requests.title: Limine review round: a real GRUB check and a single rollback
pull_requests.head: ca098e5dbbcd761d67fdd7144a33c6b3e6165b0a

commits.message:
Limine review round: a real GRUB check and a single rollback

The installer accepted a GRUB configuration that merely mentioned the
kernel's file names; it now requires a linux directive naming the kernel
image and an initrd directive naming its initramfs, and the VM harness
checks Omarchy's output the same way. A declined activation returns
success instead of an error that fired the rollback a second time through
the trap. The leaf's tests no longer move the checkout's own menu
template, and the rollback case now fails a step the leaf does not guard.

pull_requests.title: Apple Silicon: the runtime works on a Mac with no GRUB
pull_requests.head: 1b994dcfcc2e32dc9a4411787d529bb8080a9570

commits.message:
Apple Silicon: the runtime works on a Mac with no GRUB

Step one towards an image that ships Limine: nothing on a Limine Mac may
require GRUB. The fresh installer requires the boot loader its image
carries and verifies the boot chain when Limine is active, the bundle
update accepts a Limine menu, the console leaf writes the command line
either way but regenerates GRUB only where it exists, the boot update
refreshes GRUB's unused image only when it is installed, and the two GRUB
migrations no-op on a Limine Mac.

No-GRUB runtime: test GRUB itself, and judge Limine without the runtime

update-grub ships with asahi-scripts, which stays for update-m1n1, so its
presence says nothing about GRUB; the leaf, the console leaf, the quiet
migration and the boot update now look for grub-probe and grub-mkconfig.
The installer's Limine predicate reads the ESP the image shipped, so an
install interrupted before the runtime lands still resumes.

pull_requests.title: Limine leaf: keep the installer's staging directory, reset another identity's menu
pull_requests.head: d418ab7f95e8ba447df4fb368ddd838a5ffc7943

commits.message:
Limine leaf: keep the installer's staging directory, reset another identity's menu

The leaf deleted /boot/efi/omarchy, which is where the macOS installer
writes install.conf, and it kept a menu whose entries belong to another
machine-id: the image's, or the one from before a factory reset. Those
entries point at a UKI this Mac does not have. The menu now starts over
from the template in that case, and the stale identity's history on the
ESP goes with it.

pull_requests.title: omarchy-mac-boot: let update-grub write the ESP the encrypt unit holds read-only
pull_requests.head: 4082944420da7d337fd5dd32609a1f5a73020aa1

commits.message:
omarchy-mac-boot: let update-grub write the ESP the encrypt unit holds read-only

The initrd unit reads install.conf from a read-only mount of the ESP. When it
finishes a fresh conversion it runs update-grub in the opened root, and
asahi-scripts' mount_boot_esp bind-mounts /boot/efi, which is that same mount,
so copying BOOTAA64.EFI failed with a read-only file system and the boot stopped
at "Dependency failed for Initrd Root Device". Seen on the first encrypted first
boot of a built image in a KVM guest; an installed Mac never ran this path.

The finish step now remounts the ESP read-write before the chroot and hands it
back read-only afterwards. The test stub of update-grub writes under
/boot/efi/EFI/BOOT and the conversion case runs with the ESP fixture read-only.
test: the update-grub stub writes with a builtin only (the chroot has no coreutils)

omarchy-mac-boot: order sd-encrypt's Boot key mount after the encrypt unit

On the boot after a conversion the cmdline carries rd.luks.key=…:UUID=<Boot>.
The generator's key-device mount takes the Boot partition read-only the moment
its node appears, while the unit still holds it read-write to read
encrypt.state and open the root with the throwaway key. ext4 refuses the second
mount, systemd-cryptsetup@root fails on its key mount, and emergency.target
stops the unit in the middle of cryptsetup open: the guest landed in the
emergency shell on its second boot.

A drop-in in the initramfs orders run-systemd-cryptsetup-keydev\x2droot.mount
after omarchy-mac-encrypt.service; the unit releases the partition when it is
done and systemd-cryptsetup finds the mapping already open.
omarchy-mac-boot: hand the ESP back read-only only when it was read-only
test: match the key-mount drop-in path with a single backslash
omarchy-mac-boot: restore the ESP on cleanup too; test clears a stale probe
omarchy-mac-boot 20260921-5: initrd encrypt fixes

pull_requests.title: Mac image: ship Limine, its menu and the UKI
pull_requests.head: 68a61cef1aba768c6aae20a0feda2a42e19de6e8

commits.message:
Mac image: ship Limine, its menu and the UKI

The image activates Limine the same way an installed Mac does, so a Mac
boots m1n1, U-Boot and Limine from the moment the install finishes, with
no GRUB menu on the first boot or after it. GRUB stays installed for
/etc/default/grub, where the kernel command line lives, and its image is
kept off the U-Boot slot at /boot/grub/grub-aa64.efi. The image check
requires Limine in the slot, the Omarchy menu, and a UKI the menu boots.

Mac image: run the activation, and ship no identity of the builder

The builder exports OMARCHY_MAC_IMAGE_BUILD, which every hardware leaf
declines on, so the activation never ran; it is cleared for this one leaf.
limine-entry-tool gives the image's empty machine-id a value and keys its
history on the ESP by it: the identity is scrubbed again after activation,
that history removed, and the installer's staging directory recreated. The
image check reads the kernel entry Limine boots and the UKI's sections
instead of matching strings anywhere in the file.
